_doc: Footprint COURTYARD-CENTRE positions in board-relative mm (outline origin top-left, 140x110), [x, y, rot]. Applied by tools/apply_placement.py.
_plan: ESP32 rot 270, centred at (80,38): audio pin row along the top at y=25.3 (5V at the left end, 3V3 at the right), UI row along the bottom at y=50.7. The module stands on sockets, so the 57 x 22 mm under it is free routing space -- reachable only from the left and right edges of the courtyard, because the two pad rows are 2.54 mm pitch and no track fits between adjacent pads. DIR9001 socket on the right edge with its three series terminators in the open band below it, so the ten socket pads fan out without anything in the channel. DACs on the left, header columns facing the ESP32, output pads facing the edge terminals. Each DAC's bead+cap filter sits in the band below the ESP32 beside the DAC it feeds. Surround TRS terminals on the bottom edge with their 100 R series network in a row directly above, each resistor in line with the jack pad it feeds, so no two output traces cross. The 5 V parts are pushed hard against the top edge to leave a second route from the top pad row to the DACs, over the module rather than under it. Bottom edge: encoder, OLED, and the status LED on IO4 -- a bottom-row pin, so it does not drag a trace across the board from the far end of the top row. Nothing is placed in the strip x 47..51.5: that is the only vertical corridor between the DAC header columns and the rest of the board, and the two clock nets have to run down it to reach both DACs.
